text: Not a mountain with a peak. Not a slow river of lava.
A crater so wide, you could drive across it for almost an hour… without knowing you were inside.
But here is what keeps scientists watching it.
Beneath it lies a chamber of hot, partly molten rock big enough to fill the Grand Canyon more than twice.
And it has exploded before. Three times.
The ground would start to tremble. Not once… hundreds of times a day.
Rising magma could push the earth upwards, tilting roads until they crack open.
Steam and boiling water would burst out of the ground where yesterday there were only trees.
Sirens. Every road out of the park is full.
Then, for a moment, the shaking stops.
But deep below, the pressure is still rising.
